newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0/11.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0/11.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 10.0/11.0 percent on Wednesday on flush supply amid a neutral central bank money policy, dealers said.
They said call money was little changed since the morning, suggesting sufficient liquidity was available in the market, which also kept longer-term rates softer.

One-week money was at 12.75/13.00 percent and one-month was at 13.25/13.375 percent. But longer-term swaps were steady following offshore covering due to worries over the ongoing campaign for the May 29 general election, dealers said.
Dealers said operators remained cautious in anticipation of a tighter rupiah market on Friday for weekly tax payments after a smaller than expected amount was delivered on Tuesday.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates unchanged, with one-week bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 14.39 percent, compared with 14.26 percent on Monday.

Bond dealers said prices were little changed. One bond dealer said some investors were disappointed on the seven-year 500 billion rupiah issue of Bank DKI whose coupon was cut by 50 basis points to 15.0 percent on heavy over-subscription.
